rule.description: An ordinary `if` expression whose condition evaluates to a fixed boolean at compile time because it is built from same-crate constant boolean items (optionally negated, combined with `&&`/`||`, or short-circuited against a runtime subexpression), leaving one side of the branch permanently unreachable while the code still compiles and behaves as if the branch did not exist.

checks.description: Report every `if` expression in the analyzed crates whose condition is const-resolvable to a fixed boolean through a chain of same-crate `const` items (including `!` negation, `&&`/`||` combination, and short-circuit combinations with runtime subexpressions), and name the side of the branch that is therefore permanently unreachable.
checks.detected_relation: compile-time-constant guard condition -> permanently unreachable branch body
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The unreachable branch body is dead code by construction: it can never execute at runtime, yet it is still compiled, read, and maintained. Removing the dead side (and the helpers reachable only through it) is a pure dead-code elimination that leaves observable behavior identical.

matches.evidence: Dylint match at 29:69: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_MOCK_FORMAT && prompt.to_text().len() < 96` const-evaluates to `false` because the left operand of `&&` resolves to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_MOCK_FORMAT` (defined in the same module); short-circuit semantics make the then branch unreachable regardless of the runtime length check.

Dylint match at 175:83: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_TOKEN_ACCOUNTING` resolves to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_TOKEN_ACCOUNTING` (declared in the same module), so the legacy tuple `(0, 0)` selection in the then branch can never execute; the live `gpt-3.5`-aware tuple selection runs instead.

Dylint match at 87:38: condition `EMIT_LEGACY_MODEL_ALIASES` resolves to the constant false `EMIT_LEGACY_MODEL_ALIASES` (declared in the same module), making the legacy `openai/`-prefixed alias formatting in the then branch permanently unreachable; the plain model-name rendering always runs.

Dylint match at 31:35: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_ROLE_MAPPING` resolves to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_ROLE_MAPPING` (declared in the same module); the legacy role-collapsing arm in the then branch (which mapped Assistant and System roles together) can never execute.

Dylint match at 61:16: condition `UNIFIED_EMBEDDINGS_PARSING` resolves to the constant true `UNIFIED_EMBEDDINGS_PARSING` (declared in the same module), so the else branch holding the legacy collect-all-then-truncate-to-1536 parsing is permanently unreachable.

Dylint match at 95:39: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_CONTEXT_TRIM` resolves through the `crate::legacy` module to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_CONTEXT_TRIM`; the then branch calling `trim_to_max_messages(legacy_trim_target(tokens_remaining))` is permanently unreachable, so the live `trim_context` path always executes.

Dylint match at 59:42: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_STREAM_ASSEMBLY` resolves through the `crate::legacy` module to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_STREAM_ASSEMBLY`; the legacy segment-reassembly block in the then branch is permanently unreachable and the live single-pass assembly always runs.

Dylint match at 135:41: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_YAML_FENCE_PARSING` resolves through the `crate::legacy` module to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_YAML_FENCE_PARSING`; the then branch scanning fenced ```text blocks is permanently unreachable, so the live final-code-fence extraction always runs.

Dylint match at 121:16: condition `!RETAIN_LEGACY_PROMPT_PIPELINE` const-evaluates to `true` through a three-item chain: `RETAIN_LEGACY_PROMPT_PIPELINE` is derived as `RETAIN_LEGACY_PROMPT_COMBINE && RETAIN_LEGACY_CONTEXT_TRIM`, both of which resolve to constant false in `crate::legacy`; the negated condition is therefore fixed true and the else branch holding the legacy chat-append path is permanently unreachable.

Dylint match at 191:41: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_TOKEN_SPLITTER` resolves through the `crate::legacy` module to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_TOKEN_SPLITTER`; the early-return legacy chunking loop in the then branch is permanently unreachable, so the live stride-based splitting always executes.

Dylint match at 93:44: condition `RETAIN_LEGACY_TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS` resolves through the `crate::legacy` module to the constant false `RETAIN_LEGACY_TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS`; the then branch building the legacy plain-text tool listing is permanently unreachable, so the live serde_yaml serialization always runs.

excluded: The `std::env::var("LLM_CHAIN_LEGACY_TRIM_BUDGET")` match in `Chain::send_message_raw` (crates/llm-chain/src/chains/conversation.rs): its outcome depends on the runtime environment, not on any compile-time constant, so it is deliberately outside the rule even though it selects between trimming strategies.

Runtime-value-dependent branches such as `if tool_invocations.len() > 1` (crates/llm-chain/src/tools/collection.rs) and `if !current_body.is_empty()` (crates/llm-chain/src/output/stream.rs): the analyzed condition is not const-resolvable, so both sides remain reachable.

Platform/build-configuration gating via `#[cfg(...)]` attributes and feature flags: configuration-dependent compilation is not an `if` expression with a constant-guarded condition and is intentionally not reported under this rule.
API deprecation markers such as the `#[deprecated]` model variants in crates/llm-chain-openai/src/chatgpt/model.rs: deprecated-but-callable code is not a never-taken branch.

The constant switch items themselves and the helper functions called only from unreachable branches: they belong to the same injected constellation as the guarded branches rather than constituting separate branch-reachability matches.
